📸 Pensión Mujeres Bienestar — Quiroga, Michoacán · 4 de julio de 2026

🇲🇽✊ A pension that finally names the work women have always done without pay: care. "Las mujeres hemos hecho en toda esta historia... un trabajo que a veces no es reconocido... el trabajo de cuidados." "Throughout this whole history, we women have done work that often goes unrecognized — the work of care." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Quiroga, Michoacán · July 4, 2026 146,158 women in Michoacán already receive the Pensión Mujeres Bienestar, which Welfare official Leticia Ramírez called "an act of justice." It covers ages 60–64 — the gap years before the universal senior pension — treating a lifetime of caregiving as labor owed recognition.

🇲🇽✊ One trillion pesos, paid straight to the people — through a public bank, not private intermediaries. "Estamos destinando este año un billón de pesos directo al pueblo de México a través de su banco, el banco del pueblo, el Banco del Bienestar." "This year we are channeling one trillion pesos directly to the people of Mexico through their own bank — the people's bank, the Banco del Bienestar." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Quiroga, Michoacán · July 4, 2026 Pensions and scholarships are deposited straight into recipients' accounts at the state-owned Banco del Bienestar, bypassing the private banks and middlemen that historically skimmed social spending.

🇲🇽✊ "Women are people, and we have every right." "Las mujeres somos personas y tenemos todos los derechos: el derecho a educarnos, el derecho a trabajar, el derecho al acceso a la salud especial para las mujeres." "Women are people, and we have every right: the right to educate ourselves, the right to work, the right to healthcare made for women." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Pensión Mujeres Bienestar event, Quiroga, Michoacán · July 4, 2026 The Pensión Mujeres Bienestar pays women aged 60–64 until they reach the universal senior pension at 65 — a public benefit built around the years of unpaid work the state never counted before.

🇲🇽🐉🌐 Mexico Rules Out a China Trade Deal — But Keeps the Line Open

On July 2, Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard confirmed Mexico is not pursuing a free trade agreement with China while the T-MEC review is underway. "Mexico is not promoting new agreements at this time," he said — the priority is defending access to the US market, which absorbs roughly 80% of Mexican exports. China remains Mexico's second-largest trading partner, with a trade balance that runs heavily in Beijing's favor.

But ruling out an FTA is not slamming the door. Ebrard signaled that dialogue with China on tariffs will continue throughout 2026 — Mexico levies duties on Chinese goods to answer US pressure on rules of origin, yet keeps the channel open instead of picking a side. That is the entire strategy: protect the market that pays the bills today, without surrendering the leverage a second and third partner give you tomorrow.

Washington wants Mexico to choose. Mexico is choosing Mexico — defending the US market while refusing to become anyone's instrument against Beijing.

🇲🇽🔥🌐 The US Won't Renew the T-MEC. Mexico and Canada Already Signed 16 More Years.

On July 1, the Trump administration declined to extend the USMCA/T-MEC for another 16-year term — even though Mexico and Canada both signed on through 2042. Instead of stability, Washington triggered Article 34.7.4: an annual review every single year until the pact expires in 2036, with a third round of bilateral talks already scheduled for Mexico City the week of July 20. Trump's stated grievance is the US trade deficit. His own words: "we don't need anything that Mexico has."

The message from Washington is permanent uncertainty. The answer from Mexico is arithmetic. Some $872.8 billion in Mexico–US trade moved in 2025, nearly all of it tariff-free — but a partner who reopens the deal every 12 months and brags that he doesn't need you is not one you build an entire economy around. Sheinbaum kept the treaty alive AND kept every other door open: the EU treaty, Latin American integration, dialogue with Asia.

Sovereignty isn't loyalty to a single market that threatens you on a schedule. It's refusing to let any one capital hold your future hostage.

🇲🇽🏭 GUANAJUATO CLEARS $10 BILLION IN A SINGLE QUARTER

Guanajuato exported 10,020 million dollars in Q1 2026 — up 9.8% year-on-year, sixth among all Mexican states — with manufacturing at 96.6% of the total and autos and auto parts leading at 70.9%, per INEGI data. The shipping wasn't done by a handful of giants: 1,418 exporting companies, 78% of them micro, small and mid-sized firms, reached 113 countries.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 MEXICO CITY MARCHES FOR VENEZUELA

Outside the US Embassy in Mexico City, the Anti-imperialist and Anti-fascist Front demanded freedom for Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores — held for six months — and an end to the 1,300-plus coercive measures strangling Venezuela as it digs out from the June 24 earthquake. "Los queremos de vuelta" — we want them back — they chanted at the embassy gates.

🔥🇲🇽 THE SOFT-COUP PLAYBOOK GOES LIVE DURING THE WORLD CUP

With Mexico hosting the World Cup, Contralínea documents a real-time disinformation operation pushing "failed state" and "narco-government" narratives to pressure FIFA into moving matches out of the country. The named operatives aren't even Mexican: Argentina's Fernando Cerimedo of La Derecha Diario, tied to Brazil's electoral-fraud networks, and Spain's Javier Negre, convicted in Spanish court for fabricating news.
